clue.text: Disclose what offers kept a reserve

indicators.note: read as re-serve, to serve up again in a fresh arrangement, so the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shop discloses which special offers were held back in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reserve' looks like a noun, but read as re-serve it is the anagram signal for the fifteen letters of 'what offers kept a'.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove the covering from something is an idiom for revealing it publicly.

clue.text: Love someone who left hot drink out

definitions.note: the phrase takes an object, as love does someone

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters of the preceding words get rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sweet on a person who walked off leaving a hot drink behind.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to hold a person in the very highest affection and esteem.

clue.text: Jack found in church, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the word wanted only sounds like the one clued

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church

explanation.surface: A man called Jack was discovered inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: The silent K means the playing card and the church's central aisle are said the same.
explanation.definitionFit: In a pack of cards the jack is also called the knave.

clue.text: Passing through Turkish capital, changing trains

indicators.note: the capital, or head letter, of the word Turkish is wanted
changing tells us the letters of trains are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller passing through Ankara has to change trains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkish capital' suggests Ankara, but it is only the capital letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in transit is a state of being on the way through somewhere.

clue.text: Understanding French

parts.note: looks like someone who speaks the language, but means the French word for an understanding

explanation.surface: Someone who has a grasp of the French language.
explanation.definitionFit: The French loanword is used for a friendly agreement between nations, a diplomatic accord.

clue.text: Unusual portion of toasted cheese

parts.note: rare means unusual
a bit is a portion

explanation.surface: An odd helping of cheese on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is a British dish of melted cheese on toast.

clue.text: It's one after another

parts.note: sounds like a sequence of events, but describes someone chasing another person

explanation.surface: Things happening in quick succession.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaser goes after somebody else, literally one following another.

clue.text: Start to speak without a single drink

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the speaking word goes round the rest

parts.note: to orate is to speak formally
a single is one, the Roman numeral I
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: Begin talking without having had a single drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it has its old sense of outside, so the speaking word encloses the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To originate is to begin or come into being, a synonym of start.

clue.text: Improvident way to eat

parts.note: literally food passed straight from palm to lips, figuratively living with nothing saved

explanation.surface: A careless, wasteful style of eating.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes spending everything as soon as it comes, with no provision for the future.

clue.text: I can't earn redress, as race won easily

indicators.note: read as re-dress, to dress again, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint from someone unable to earn compensation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redress' seems to mean compensation, but read as re-dress it signals rearranging 'I can't earn'.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse winning at a canter wins without needing to gallop, so effortlessly.

clue.text: Creature developing one horn

indicators.note: developing suggests change of form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An animal that is growing a single horn, like a unicorn.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhinoceros is a large animal, often with a single horn on its snout.

clue.text: Continues to pay for the boy

parts.note: to keep someone is to pay for their upkeep
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A parent goes on supporting their lad financially.
explanation.definitionFit: Persisting with something is to carry on doing it, a phrasal verb synonym.

clue.text: Cruel animal brush, it should be thrown out

indicators.note: thrown out suggests disorder, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A grooming brush used harshly on a pet ought to be binned.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutish describes a person who is savage and coarse, like a beast.

clue.text: Language establishing an audible bond

indicators.note: audible means the word as heard, so a soundalike is wanted

parts.note: a tie is a bond

explanation.surface: Language that creates a bond you can hear.
explanation.definitionFit: Tai is a family of languages of Southeast Asia, including Thai and Lao.

clue.text: He often resorts to a piece in colour

indicators.note: the words before in go inside the colour word

parts.note: a hue is a colour
a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: A man who keeps going on holiday to resorts, sporting a bit of colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resorts' suggests holiday spots, but here it is a verb: he resorts to, or frequents, a place.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitue is a regular visitor who frequents a particular place.

clue.text: Exploded with fury, where there's commission to pay

parts.note: broke as a storm or wave bursts
rage is fury

explanation.surface: Someone flew into a rage over the fees they were charged.
explanation.definitionFit: A broker's business, or the fee charged by an agent, which is a commission.

clue.text: Avail oneself of sheep, we hear

indicators.note: indicates a word that sounds like the one clued

parts.note: ewes are female sheep

explanation.surface: A farmer taking advantage of the flock, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail oneself of something is to make use of it, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Country with rain after winter's half gone

indicators.note: after puts the rain word behind the shortened season
the first half of the word is removed, leaving its last three letters

parts.note: the word winter, with its possessive ending as a link

explanation.surface: Land soaked with rain once half the winter has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half gone' removes the first half of the season, and 'after' places the weather word behind what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is a stretch of land and its physical features, as country means open land.

clue.text: Some of the musicians get the bird

indicators.note: some of says the answer is part of the following words' letters

explanation.surface: Several players are booed off stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get the bird' is an idiom for being jeered, which disguises the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The emu is a large flightless Australian bird.

clue.text: Exclamation partygoers may make

parts.note: a cry of delight at a party, plus the idiom to make ..., meaning to celebrate wildly

explanation.surface: Something revellers shout at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a shout of joy, and making it is an idiom for noisy celebration.

clue.text: Entrance for the colliery boss?

parts.note: a colliery is a coal pit
a head is a boss

explanation.surface: The door used by the manager of a coal mine.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the whole clue also reads as a joke about the mine's chief.
explanation.definitionFit: The top of a mine shaft and its buildings is where miners go in to work.

clue.text: Singular mistake in Latin translation

parts.note: looks like an odd translating blunder, but asks for the Latin singular word for one mistake

explanation.surface: A remarkable blunder made while translating Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for an error, the singular of errata, used for a printing mistake.

clue.text: American small change being found in school is dodgy

indicators.note: the American and the coin are placed inside the school

parts.note: a sect is a school of thought
P is a penny, small British change

explanation.surface: Small American coins turning up in a school look questionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something suspect is open to suspicion, of doubtful honesty, so shady.

clue.text: Starts out and trips

definitions.meaning: triggers, as an alarm is set going

explanation.surface: Someone begins a walk and stumbles.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to begin a journey and to trigger something.

clue.text: Puts off one's retirement

parts.note: sounds like delaying leaving work, but means delaying going to bed

explanation.surface: Someone postpones leaving their job.
explanation.definitionFit: Retiring for the night means going to bed, so delaying it is remaining awake late.

clue.text: Some very early cereal

indicators.note: some marks part of the following words as the answer

explanation.surface: A little breakfast eaten at dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is a grain crop grown for flour and whisky.

clue.text: Appear on stage again in a more entertaining way

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the following words

explanation.surface: An actor makes another entrance in a livelier manner.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor entering the stage a second time comes back on, so returns.

clue.text: It may appear smart on the stern of a boat

indicators.note: the letters may show up in another form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something that looks smart painted on the back of a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may appear' signals rearranging the letters of 'smart on'.
explanation.definitionFit: A transom is the flat surface forming the back end of a vessel's hull.

clue.text: Setting for a confrontation?

definitions.meaning: the place where action is set
a noisy public row, as in making a fuss

explanation.surface: A stage set built for a showdown.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the location of action and an angry public outburst.

clue.text: Sailor died a dissolute man

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute man

explanation.surface: A seaman died a debauched man.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Francis Drake was the Elizabethan seafarer who sailed around the world.

clue.text: Clothes not a single woman will go out in

definitions.text: Clothes not a single woman will go out in

parts.words: Clothes not a single woman will go out in
parts.note: sounds as if no woman would wear them, but means a bride, no longer single, wears them

explanation.surface: Garments so dreadful no woman would wear them outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's collection of clothes and linen for married life, worn once she is no longer single.

clue.text: Say what you like, this right is not protected everywhere

definitions.text: Say what you like, this right is not protected everywhere

parts.words: Say what you like, this right is not protected everywhere
parts.note: reads as a concession in an argument, but describes the civil liberty to say anything

explanation.surface: A grudging admission that a liberty isn't universal.
explanation.definitionFit: The civil liberty to express opinions without censorship, guaranteed in some countries only.
